name: OpenWork v0.18.63
body:
## Bring Claude conversations into OpenWork

- **Bring your Claude history with you.** Import Claude chats and Claude Code sessions into a workspace from Settings → Import, where they become regular OpenWork chats.
- **Work with connected files on OpenCode v2.** Bring Google Drive, OneDrive, and SharePoint files into your workspace and save edits back; attach workspace files to Gmail drafts and replies, or upload them to Google Drive. OpenWork asks you to approve each transfer.
- **Use computer use on Windows and set it up once.** Windows desktop users can use computer use with apps on This PC. Set it up in Settings → Computer use; chats no longer have a computer status button, and the browser has one button in the side rail.
- **Desktop work keeps its place and gets easier to start.** The window reopens at its previous size and position, Cmd+N (Ctrl+N) starts a session even while you type, and organization switching refreshes your skills, connected apps, and models. Verified sign-in no longer waits for organization discovery to finish. Show model reasoning now starts off; turn it on in Settings → Preferences to see readable reasoning.
- **For admins: completed features are now available by default, with clearer controls.** Local AI providers, Automation settings, agent-assisted connection removal, Workbot search, improved usage-limit cards, task-preserving sign-in, Claude imports, and organization Prompts are available without a special setup; retired OpenCode Zen models are no longer offered. Automations are on by default, with separate Desktop and Cloud controls for organizations; sandbox join links add admins by default, with a choice to add members instead.
- **Workbot, models, and self-hosted setups are more dependable.** Workbot handles brief sign-in interruptions and rebuilds outdated computers when resumed. OpenWork Models adds GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; self-hosted desktops no longer update beyond the server's supported release.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.62...v0.18.63)

*Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.*

name: v2.2.0
body:
### Highlights

- Create, install and share [Desktop plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui) (experimental) ([#55246](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55246), [#59469](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59469), [#59489](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59489))
- Refreshed the desktop app experience ([#56898](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56898), [#58865](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58865), [#55838](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55838), [#57962](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57962))
- Add experimental image and decision generation APIs to plugins and sdk, allowing image generation or decision model (think typesafe, clef, etc) workflows. ([#59190](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59190), [#59380](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59380), [#58758](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58758))
- Plugins can now attach and update keyed session instructions with ctx.session.instructions.entry.put/list/remove. Instead of editing the system prompt and busting the prompt cache, each change is added as a small update at the next step. The entries also survive compaction and reverts, and they don't start an extra model turn. ([#56550](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56550))
- Restored the Todo tool in desktop via opt-in ([#59092](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59092))
- Add configurable prompt cache TTLs per provider/model ([#59157](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59157))

### Breaking changes

#### `@opencode/ai` root is now the Promise API

`@opencode/ai` now works like `@opencode/sdk` and `@opencode/client`: the package root exports the Promise API, and the Effect API moved to `@opencode/ai/effect`. `@opencode/ai/promise` is removed, and the wildcard subpath export is replaced with an explicit list of provider and protocol entry points. ([#58847](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58847), [#59183](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59183))

```diff
-import { AI } from "@opencode/ai/promise"
-import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { AI } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai/effect"
```

#### The OpenCode GitHub Action is removed

The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published. Remove it from your workflows. ([#59032](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59032))

#### TUI plugins require OpenTUI 0.7

`@opencode/plugin` now requires `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.7.0, up from 0.6.8 or later. Plugins that depend on OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install until they upgrade. In OpenTUI 0.7, custom renderables read their hooks from their class at construction: assign `renderBefore`, `renderAfter`, and `onLifecyclePass` in the constructor instead of as class fields, call `refreshHooks()` after adding a hook by reflection, and replace `defineNativeIntegration()` with a `static nativeIntegration` declaration. See the [OpenTUI 0.7.0 release notes](https://opentui.com/docs/releases/0.7.0). ([#59295](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59295))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Add experimental image and decision generation API endpoints. ([#59190](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59190))
- Add image and decision entrypoints for catalog providers. ([#59380](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59380))
- Improve integration rebuild performance. ([#59402](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59402))
- Let custom model configuration set a model type. ([#59388](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59388))
- Let model-list API requests filter by type. ([#59355](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59355))
- Make external-directory permission checks use the project's filesystem. ([#59089](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59089))
- Reduce memory use when code search finds very large lines. ([#59205](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59205))
- Let plugins filter event subscriptions by type. ([#58864](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58864))
- Add configurable prompt-cache TTLs. ([#59157](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59157))
- Move image resizing off the main process and release idle image memory. ([#58820](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58820))
- Reduce repeated session-history loading during a step. ([#59091](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59091))
- Add an experimental API for session media and opt-in media URI support. ([#59103](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59103))
- Add the machine hostname to `/api/info`. ([#59090](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59090))
- Add experimental content-addressed blob storage for session media behind `experimental.media_blob`. ([#58656](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58656), [#58741](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58741))
- Start session history from the latest completed compaction. ([#59020](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59020))
- Reduce work encoding durable event payloads that are not persisted. ([#58923](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58923))
- Expose MCP server titles from `serverInfo`. ([#58950](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58950))
- Apply OpenCode Console workspace configuration as a configuration layer. ([#57703](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57703))
- Replace experimental evaluations with Decision APIs in the AI pkg, including OpenAI Decisions, System One, and Cloudflare Run models. ([#58758](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58758), [#58382](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58382), [#58379](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58379), [#58381](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58381))
- Convert tool schemas once to speed up tool execution. ([#58798](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58798), [#58848](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58848))
- Make Git project discovery faster while recognizing repository changes. ([#58616](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58616))
- Show OpenCode Console budget limits and Go usage where they block you. ([#58694](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58694), [#58714](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58714))
- Record provider-reported session costs. ([#58562](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58562))
- Find Git more reliably on macOS. ([#58602](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58602))
- Resolve model details once per prompt step. ([#58601](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58601))
- Let plugins manage session instruction entries for subsequent model requests. ([#56550](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56550))
- Add GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6.1 Terra Fast to Sign in with ChatGPT. ([#59359](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59359))

#### Bug fixes

- Wait for plugins to finish reloading before each session step and tool call. Thanks [@kernel-oops](https://github.com/kernel-oops) and [@Tarquinen](https://github.com/Tarquinen). ([#51133](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/51133))
- Size session compaction from the provider's reported token count to preserve usable context. ([#59441](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59441))
- Skip unavailable models.dev API entrypoints instead of failing model catalog updates. ([#59475](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59475))
- Return a server error with a reference ID when the server cannot encode a response. ([#59459](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59459))
- Avoid warming a session while its model request is running. ([#59325](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59325))
- Preserve legacy MCP `codemode` settings during migration. Thanks [@tneemo](https://github.com/tneemo). ([#59126](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59126))
- Use the correct Vertex AI endpoints for the `eu` and `us` multi-regions. ([#59335](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59335))
- Accept Databricks hosts that include `http://` or `https://`. ([#59334](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59334))
- Keep files intact when patch edits move a file onto itself. ([#59197](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59197))
- Preserve literal `$0` and `$ARGUMENTS` text in custom command input. ([#59198](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59198))
- Close project locations concurrently during shutdown. ([#59326](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59326))
- Treat equivalent directory paths, including trailing slashes, as one location. ([#59327](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59327))
- Send valid tool schemas to Kimi for tuple, default, and keyword-like arguments. ([#59207](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59207))
- Expose Code Mode MCP tools directly when the `execute` permission is denied. ([#59315](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59315))
- Coordinate OAuth credential refreshes across locations and processes. ([#54023](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/54023))
- List and search remote Git branches correctly without bare remote names. ([#58597](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58597))
- Detect AVIF, HEIC/HEIF, QuickTime, and M4A attachments correctly. ([#58480](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58480), [#58886](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58886), [#58887](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58887))
- Reduce memory retained by long-running tool calls and unchanged hooked model requests. ([#58448](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58448), [#58449](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58449))
- Load session diffs without reading every message, improving performance for large sessions. ([#57686](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57686))
- Keep active locations alive when session events use an equivalent directory path. ([#56259](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56259))
- Reload compatibility skills only when their own sources change. ([#59086](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59086))
- Avoid publishing redundant catalog updates when configuration is unchanged. ([#56267](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56267))
- Avoid booting idle or deleted project locations while polling session forms. ([#59083](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59083))
- Wait for plugins before returning agent and provider lists, preventing incomplete catalogs. ([#59082](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59082))
- Manage sessions and instruction entries after their project directory is deleted. ([#58997](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58997))
- Start fuzzy file search only on first use, reducing project startup work. ([#58959](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58959))
- Exit after 10 seconds when shutdown hangs and report pending work. ([#58817](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58817))
- Keep the models catalog fresh without redownloading it when unchanged. ([#58813](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58813))
- Send xAI Responses `top_k` settings and stop sending unsupported penalties. ([#58868](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58868))
- Honor shared parallel tool-call and service-tier settings for Groq. ([#58871](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58871))
- Retry throttled requests instead of misreporting them as context overflows. ([#58866](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58866))
- Preserve streamed text and reasoning that arrive after an OpenAI Chat finish reason. ([#58851](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58851))
- Classify AWS REST JSON errors consistently regardless of where the error type appears. ([#58770](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58770))
- Validate large base64 attachments without slowdowns or hangs. ([#58811](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58811))
- Retry Bedrock throttling errors as rate limits instead of context overflows. Thanks [@Irish-Joseph](https://github.com/Irish-Joseph). ([#58759](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58759))
- Keep working MCP tools available when a server returns malformed ones. ([#58350](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58350))
- Match absolute instruction-file globs across directories. Thanks [@heimoshuiyu](https://github.com/heimoshuiyu). ([#58749](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58749))
- Use configured provider regions in Bedrock endpoint URLs. ([#58538](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58538))
- Handle unknown OpenAI Chat finish reasons without failing the response. ([#58608](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58608))
- Avoid unnecessary Azure model updates when endpoint transforms make no change. ([#58600](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58600))
- Prefer JPEG for opaque browser screenshots, reducing attachment size. ([#56990](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56990))
- Detect generated image types from their bytes when compatible hosts omit the format. ([#58475](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58475))
- Keep project services alive while sessions run long tools or wait for input, with a 24-hour inactivity cap. ([#57274](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57274))
- Prevent unrelated configuration changes and compatibility-skill update bursts from repeatedly reloading skills. ([#56260](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56260))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- Reduce CPU use while animated session-tab pulses are visible. ([#59235](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59235))
- List OpenCode Console before OpenCode Go in the integration picker. ([#59107](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59107))
- Add `/usage`, model-picker, prompt, sidebar, warning, and error details for OpenCode Console usage limits. ([#58731](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58731))
- Make CLI service registration more reliable when concurrent processes update its files. ([#59105](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59105))

#### Bug fixes

- Return `opencode run --format json` server connection errors as JSON. Thanks [@andreivince](https://github.com/andreivince). ([#59366](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59366))
- Preserve pasted prompt text when copying it back out. ([#59209](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59209))
- Reliably update the background service on Windows when its files are briefly locked. ([#59105](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59105))
- Keep the background service state directory out of tool shells and identify processes blocking its port. ([#58815](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58815))

- Keep the TUI running when a plugin slot or route renders bare text. Thanks [@anmol0b](https://github.com/anmol0b) and [@Tarquinen](https://github.com/Tarquinen). ([#58144](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58144))
- Accept `--server` and `--standalone` anywhere in supported CLI commands. ([#58505](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58505))
- Release closed and background session transcripts to prevent memory growth. ([#58434](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58434), [#57025](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57025))
- Connect remote access tunnels through HTTP proxies. ([#58464](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58464))
- Keep development builds on a separate server, database, and port from released builds. ([#58331](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58331))

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- Manage desktop plugins from Settings › Extensions › Plugins. ([#59489](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59489))
- Add a persistent desktop zoom setting. ([#59277](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59277))
- Capture heap snapshots in desktop debug builds on `SIGUSR2` when explicitly enabled. ([#58317](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58317))
- Show the open session title in the browser tab. ([#59131](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59131))
- Show todowrite tasks above the composer. ([#59092](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59092))
- Load session history once when returning to a session tab. ([#59166](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59166))
- Answer questions with number keys and show multi-select choices as checkboxes. ([#58595](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58595))
- Add an always-available Add project action to the location picker. ([#57962](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57962))
- Let you rewind or fork from any message. ([#58865](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58865))
- Let you edit line comments and copy shell output. ([#58970](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58970), [#58974](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58974))

name: v2.13.5 — paywalls (2.0.0 → 2.1.0): new references/mobile-subscription-paywalls.md for consumer iOS…
body:
- **paywalls** (2.0.0 → 2.1.0): new `references/mobile-subscription-paywalls.md` for consumer iOS/Android subscription apps: the paywall after onboarding's first personalized result, hard paywall vs. freemium (RevenueCat 2026 data), yearly-first plan presentation, trials with reminders and trial length as a test, one abandon offer, dated store fees (Apple Small Business Program; Google Play's June 2026 10% + 5% split, with the 10% applying to web links; the US link-out commission still in court), the web-to-app funnel, revenue per download, and an App Store review checklist. New description triggers for mobile and subscription-app paywalls. Adapted from Blake Anderson's ai-app-playbook (MIT); his "best and cheapest" stack verdicts were left out.

name: v2.13.4 — Learnings from a batch of October 2026 posts, verified before inclusion:
body:
Learnings from a batch of October 2026 posts, verified before inclusion:

- **ads** (2.6.2 → 2.7.0): the Meta playbook adds **ad sequencing**: why order matters to Meta's ranking model, the narrow auction setup (Awareness or Engagement objective, target frequency, lifetime budget of 7+ days, 2+ ads), sizing a sequence to the flight, and the cost trade-off. The creative-research reference adds a **persistent competitor ad tracker** (weekly pulls from the Meta, Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, vision tagging, diffs, gap questions), with a caveat that ad longevity is a proxy, not proof. The Google Search playbook covers **AI Max** under the same gate as broad match. Sources: Cody Schneider, Jon Loomer, Meta Engineering.
- **ai-seo** (2.10.2 → 2.11.0): the prompt-portfolio reference adds scoring by **buying topic** and a fix-before-create sequence (Jam's AI search audit). Platform notes add Bing Webmaster Tools' **AI Performance report and grounding queries**, and Brave's submit-url page with its limits. Agent readiness adds Fern's Agent Score for developer docs.
- **prospecting** (1.3.0 → 1.4.0): signal plays adds **warm paths**: mining your own network (LinkedIn export, calendar, inbox), matching it to target accounts, paid connectors per vertical, and double opt-in intros (Cody Schneider's podcast with Super Connector).
- **video** (2.2.2 → 2.3.0): adds a **personalized video per account** workflow (component library, motion primitives, demo-flow menu, render engine, automated QA, tracker), adapted from Harvey's write-up. Drops the "recommended" label on HeyGen.
- **directory-submissions** (2.1.2 → 2.1.3): the Notion entry now reflects the Notion Marketplace's requirements (public connection with the "Any workspace" scope, which can't be changed later, plus a review that includes security).

Not incorporated: duplicating Shopping products to test images and landing pages (third-party sources call it a Shopping policy violation), agency spend anecdotes, and an unverified 50-site launch list.

name: v0.12.0
body:
The latest release of Lore, Epic Games' next-generation open source version control system.

[Quickstart](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/tutorials/quickstart/) | [Design](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/explanation/system-design/) | [Documentation](https://epicgames.github.io/lore/) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/E4SFJKRPbg)

## Quick Install

Windows
```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EpicGames/lore/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

macOS / Linux
```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EpicGames/lore/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

## Release Notes

Changes since v0.11.0.

### Features

* `lore service run` runs the Lore service in the current process until it stops (via `lore service stop` or `lore::service::quit`); Rust only, no C API equivalent
* Expired OIDC access tokens are renewed with the refresh token (RFC 6749 §6) on the next operation, without a new `lore auth login`
* `lore auth logout` (C API: `lore_auth_logout`) revokes the OIDC refresh token at the provider when it advertises a revocation endpoint (RFC 7009); a failed revocation fails the logout, after the local login is removed

### Fixes & Improvements

* `--dry-run` is now side-effect free across the CLI: no writes to the working tree, `.lore` config, branch/revision/staged/layer state, local or shared store, token store, settings, or the remote. Affected commands included `file reset`, `branch create|reset|archive`, `revision amend`, `unstage`, `layer add`, `link add`, `repository create|clone|gc`, `shared-store create`, `file obliterate`, `commit`, `branch merge into` and `auth login|logout|clear`
* `repository clone --force --dry-run`, `clone --dry-run --vfs swfs` and `clone --dry-run --use-shared-store` (when it would create the store) now fail instead of acting
* `repository verify --heal --dry-run` reports without healing
* Fixed a cross-process deadlock when several processes run commands on the same repository or shared store (e.g. concurrent `lore history`). All processes using the store must run this version
* `lore repository verify` fails on unreadable parts of the local store instead of skipping them, and heals fragments moved by a concurrent flush
* `lore stage` of several paths under a directory missing from disk stages deletes for only those paths, not the whole directory
* `lore stage --case keep` with a differently-cased directory stages files as modified under the repository's case, not as deleted, on case-sensitive file systems
* `lore branch switch <branch> <revision>` resolves a bare revision (`1234`, `@1234`) on `<branch>`, not the current branch
* TLS: reject certificates chained through compromised eMudhra intermediates (RUSTSEC-2026-0382) and drop the emSign ECC Root CA - G3, Root CA - C1 and ECC Root CA - C3 built-in roots
* TLS: abort on TLS 1.3 handshake messages at the wrong encryption level (RUSTSEC-2026-0285), prevent forced downgrade to classical key exchange (RUSTSEC-2026-0349), and redact secrets from client session debug output (RUSTSEC-2026-0346)

## Release Assets

> [!IMPORTANT]
These can be downloaded under the "Assets" section below.

### Installer
- `lore-setup` - Lore CLI Windows installer

### Binaries
- `lore` - Lore CLI
- `loreserver` - Lore Server
- `liblore` - Lore Shared Library

### Headers
- `lore.h` - Single header for `liblore` (packged with `liblore`)

### Supported Platforms
- Windows x84_64
- macOS AArch64
- Linux x86_64
- Linux AArch64 (for Graviton/Neoverse 512-tvb only)

## Lore Desktop Client

> [!IMPORTANT]
Lore Desktop Client is available as binaries only, download the installer for your platform here:

- Windows: [Lore-Desktop-Setup-x64.exe](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-Setup-x64.exe)
- macOS: [Lore-Desktop-arm64.dmg](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-arm64.dmg)
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04): [lore-desktop_amd64.deb](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/lore-desktop_amd64.deb)
- Linux (AppImage): [Lore-Desktop-x86_64.AppImage](https://releases.lore.org/desktop/releases/stable/Lore-Desktop-x86_64.AppImage)

##  ⬇️ Open Source Lore Assets Below ⬇️

body:
## What's Changed
### 🐛 Fixes

* fix(gh auth status): explain expired expiring tokens with `--no-refresh` by @babakks in [#14815](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/14815)


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cli/cli/compare/v2.103.2...v2.103.3

## Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-26.

### Enhancements

- Accept an empty `UV_RUN_RECURSION_DEPTH` as zero and report invalid values consistently ([#22814](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22814))
- Explain how to add project metadata when `uv init` finds a `pyproject.toml` without a `[project]` table ([#22916](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22916))

### Python

- Add CPython 3.11.18, 3.12.16, 3.13.18, 3.14.10, and 3.15.2 ([#22938](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22938))

### Preview features

- Detect NVIDIA GPU capabilities when selecting compatible wheel variants with `wheel-variants` ([#22690](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22690))
- Nest each module's owners in an object in `uv workspace metadata` output ([#22638](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22638))
- Report the unsupported properties required by an incompatible wheel variant ([#22719](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22719))

### Performance

- Reduce peak memory use when resolving large workspaces ([#22860](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22860), [#22863](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22863), [#22864](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22864), [#22866](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22866), [#22870](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22870))
- Reduce peak memory use when locking or upgrading large projects ([#22833](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22833), [#22834](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22834))
- Speed up redirected output from `uv export` and `uv pip compile` ([#22840](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22840))
- Reuse cached or active environments when running PEP 723 scripts without dependencies ([#21458](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21458))
- Reduce parsing overhead for build dependency and build backend settings ([#22848](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22848), [#22871](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22871), [#22879](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22879), [#22884](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22884))
- Reduce parsing overhead for project sources and workspace references ([#22880](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22880), [#22883](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22883))
- Reduce parsing overhead for cache, exclusion, cutoff, and preview settings ([#22876](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22876), [#22877](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22877), [#22878](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22878), [#22887](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22887))
- Reduce PyPI metadata parsing overhead ([#22874](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22874), [#22875](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22875))
- Speed up parsing tool receipt requirements ([#22885](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22885))

### Bug fixes

- Prevent `uv run --active --script` and `uv sync --active --script` from deleting non-virtual-environment directories ([#21464](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21464))
- Use `AMD64` for `platform_machine` when resolving for x86-64 Windows ([#22935](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22935))
- Preserve free-threaded and other non-default variants in `uv python upgrade` ([#22836](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22836))
- Allow `uv init --no-package` and `uv init --script` when `UV_INIT_BUILD_BACKEND` is set ([#22907](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22907))
- Prevent panics when rendering containment markers with local versions ([#22815](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22815))

### Documentation

- Update the Docker guide and reproduction examples to use uv 0.13.5 ([#22867](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22867))

name: pandoc 3.13
body:
I'm pleased to announce the release of pandoc 3.13,
available in the usual places:

Binary packages & changelog:
https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/tag/3.13

Source & API documentation:
http://hackage.haskell.org/package/pandoc-3.13

This release fixes some regressions and makes many minor
improvements.  See the changelog for full details.

Behavior changes:

- Locations of errors in default files are now reported.
- YAML is now parsed with the yamlet library, which implements
  YAML 1.2. As a result, we'll get better error messages, and:

  + `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y` and `n` are strings, not booleans.
  + Duplicate keys in a mapping are an error. They were a warning.
  + `.5`, `.inf` and `.nan` are numbers.

  The most likely way this change will bite you is if you use
  `no` in a boolean field. This will be interpreted as a nonempty
  value, which will be treated as truthy in a template.

API changes:

- Text.Pandoc.Sharde: export `plainToPara` and `paraToPlain`.
- Text.Pandoc.Writers.Shared: export new functions `wrapColumns` and
  `rendereWithTemplate`.
- Text.Pandoc.Translations: `readTranslations` now takes the path
  of the file as argument.

Thanks to all who contributed, especially new contributors
Andrzej Rybczak, Patrick Creighton, Wleeaf, and enieuwy.

<details>
  <summary>Click to expand changelog</summary>

- Report the location of errors in defaults files (#8759, Andrzej Rybczak). An invalid value in a defaults file gave an error at the start of the file, with no indication of the field. The error now names the option and points at its value.

- Use yamlet for YAML parsing. Pandoc parsed YAML with the yaml package, which depends on the C library libyaml. It now uses yamlet, a pure Haskell YAML 1.2 parser. Values still go through the existing aeson instances. Note these behavior changes:

  - `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y` and `n` are strings, not booleans, as in YAML 1.2.
  - YAML errors now show the file, the line and the column, with the offending line. In metadata blocks the line is the line in the document.
  - Duplicate keys in a mapping are an error. They were a warning.
  - `.5`, `.inf` and `.nan` are numbers.

- Docx reader:

  - Read `w:fldSimple` fields (#11944, Aslak Hellesøy).
  - Keep grid columns that have no width (#11989, Patrick Creighton). `w:w` is optional on `w:gridCol`, but `elemToTblGrid` skipped the grid columns that had none. The table then had fewer columns than its rows had cells, and the extra cells were dropped. Every grid column is now kept. If any of them has no (readable) width, all columns get the default width.
  - Fix namespaces in notes and comments (#11991, Patrick Creighton). The contents of footnotes, endnotes and comments were read with the namespace prefixes declared in word/document.xml rather than in their own parts.
  - Records the indentation of each list level and track the open list levels; an unnumbered paragraph whose left indentation matches the text indentation of an open level is treated as a continuation of that level’s current item, rather than as a block quote (cf. #9197).
  - Recover from fields with a missing instruction (#11943, enieuwy). This fixes a bug that could lead to content being omitted.
  - Fix regression (from 3.11) in parsing column widths (#11969). The regression caused only the first column to get assigned its alignment; every other column received default alignment. In addition, in 3.11 alignment was taken from the header row if present; this changed behavior from earlier versions, which took it from the first body row. We revert to the earlier behavior, using the header row only if there are no body rows. It’s common for the header to have different alignment than the rest.
  - Keep tracked paragraph marks inside notes (#11971, Aslak Hellesøy).

- RST reader:

  - Allow inline markup and bare links after `:`, `/`, `'`, `"`, `<` (Wleeaf). Fixes a regression since 3.2.1; these characters could no longer precede an inline markup start-string or a bare URI or email address, although the reStructuredText spec allows them. Also implement the rule that a start-character between an opening character and its closing counterpart, as in `(*)` or `"*"`, does not trigger inline markup.

- RTF reader:

  - Fix tokenization bug (#11981). We were consuming certain symbols after `\uNNNN` during tokenization. This led to an *extra* character being consumed as the “fallback,” so letters went missing after encoded unicode characters.

- LaTeX reader:

  - Detect macro expansion loops across `doMacros` calls (#11088).

- ODT reader:

  - Fix start numbers with `text:continue-numbering` (#9595).

- Markdown writer:

  - Write wide tables as grid tables instead of falling back to HTML (#11945, Aslak Hellesøy).
  - Don’t drop notes in notes.
  - Fix regression with code block language (#11987). We try to identify which class is a language name and emit that as the gfm style info string. If none of the classes match a recognized language, before 3.10.1 we emitted the first class; fater 3.10.1, we emit nothing. This commit reverts to the pre-3.10.1 behavior.

- RST writer:

  - Don’t drop notes in notes.

- Haddock writer:

  - Don’t drop notes in notes.

- Docx writer:

  - Fix multi-paragraph list items (#9197). Previously the docx writer gave the second and subsequent paragraphs of a list item numbering from a separate list with an invisible bullet. This looked right, but semantically these paragraphs were items of another list, which is what Word, screen readers, and pandoc’s own docx reader saw; the list was also split in three. The writer now gives these paragraphs no numbering, just an indentation that lines them up with the text of the list item (as Word’s “List Continue” styles do).

- LaTeX writer:

  - Use braces around term containing `=` (#11954). This is needed for the new LaTeX list code, which is triggered by using `pdfstandard`.

- PowerPoint writer:

  - Add `clrMapOvr` to notes slides (#11935, Gaurav Vijay Jadhav). This makes them importable by Keynote.
  - Include `lang` in core document properties.

- DocBook, JATS, TEI writers:

  - Apply `writerIdentifierPrefix` prefix consistently.

- Typst writer:

  - Escape `...` and `-?` ligatures (#11979).
  - Use `getLang` to determine lang and region. Previously only the `lang` metadata field was consulted, so `lang` could not be set properly using a variable.

- Text.Pandoc.Translations:

  - `readTranslations` now takes the path of the file, for error messages \[API change\].

- Text.Pandoc.Writers.Shared:

  - Add `wrapColumns`, `renderWithTemplate` \[API change\]. These factor out code that was repeated in about 20 writers: computing the line length from writerWrapText/writerColumns, and rendering the body with or without the template.

- Text.Pandoc.Shared:

  - Export `plainToPara` and `paraToPlain`. \[API change\]

- Text.Pandoc.PDF:

  - Make `--presentational-hints` default for weasyprint. This is necessary to get list attributes (start, ordered list type, etc.) working properly (#11976).

- cabal.project:

  - Use bundle C option for zlib by default. This allows pandoc to be built without first installing the C library zlib. Those who want to use the system zlib can still compile pandoc that way by overriding this setting in cabal.project.local, or just installing directly from Hackage.
  - Default to `+http` on GHC \>= 9.14 (previously done only in CI), so local builds behave the same; `-f-http` still overrides it.
  - Pass wasm link flags for `pandoc-cli` as `ghc-options`. cabal only passes ld-options along when it finds an `ld` program on the PATH. In an environment without one (e.g. `nix shell` with just the ghc-wasm-meta toolchain), the flags were silently dropped and linking pandoc.wasm failed with undefined `setjmp` and clock symbols. Use `-optl- ghc-options` instead, which GHC passes to its linker regardless.

- Makefile:

  - Add `release` target.
  - Improve `make pandoc-templates` so it does the whole job.
  - Use bash as `SHELL` (`check-cabal` uses `pushd`, `check-version-sync` uses `==`).
  - Fix `$(id -u)` in `debpkg`, which make expanded to empty.
  - Fix missing `echo` in `validate-docx-golden-tests{,2}`.
  - Ensure pandoc is built before rules that run it to produce files.
  - Use `git ls-files` for `SOURCEFILES`, not the main branch’s tree.
  - Drop redundant `embed_data_files` flag in `quick-stack`.

- Use released citeproc 0.14.1.1, texmath 0.13.3.3, gridtables 0.1.1.1 (#9085).

- MANUAL.txt:

  - Clarify the effect of `raw_html` in commonmark formats (#8305).

- Bump bounds on crypton, crypton-x509-system, tasty-bench.

- Add `tools/circleci-build-release.sh`, `tools/github-build-release.sh`.

</details>

name: v0.5.2.1
body:
## 中文

本次 hotfix 主要解决 **向 Session 添加消息时，隐私自动识别存在误判，导致部分普通内容被错误替换为隐私占位符，并产生无效隐私记录** 的问题。

### 主要修复：暂时关闭 Session 隐私自动识别

暂时关闭新敏感值的自动识别与替换，避免继续误替换消息内容。例如，未登记的 `password=example-password` 现在会保持原样，不再自动创建 Session 隐私记录。此调整在代码中生效，无需修改配置。([#6680](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6680))

已登记隐私值的匹配与替换仍然保留，历史隐私占位符也继续支持读取还原。本次不会清理此前产生的隐私记录。

### 其他修复

- 将 SDK 最低依赖版本提升至 `0.1.17`，修复 Compile 所需 SDK 接口缺失的问题。([#6596](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6596))
- 修复 MySQL 多服务任务隔离及旧 API 兼容性问题。([#6676](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6676))

## English

This hotfix primarily addresses **false positives in automatic Session privacy detection, which could replace ordinary message content with privacy placeholders and create invalid privacy records**.

### Main fix: temporarily disable automatic Session privacy discovery

Automatic discovery and replacement of new sensitive values are temporarily disabled to prevent further incorrect replacements when adding messages to a Session. For example, an unregistered `password=example-password` now remains unchanged and no longer creates a Session privacy entry. This change takes effect in code and requires no configuration changes. ([#6680](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6680))

Matching and replacement of already registered privacy values remain active, and historical privacy placeholders can still be restored on reads. Previously created privacy records are not removed by this release.

### Other fixes

- Raise the minimum SDK dependency to `0.1.17` to provide the SDK APIs required by Compile. ([#6596](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6596))
- Fix MySQL task isolation across services and preserve legacy API compatibility. ([#6676](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6676))

**完整变更记录 / Full Changelog:** [v0.5.2 → v0.5.2.1](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/compare/v0.5.2...v0.5.2.1)

name: v15.3.0
body:
## What changed

### Deliverables on the My Work card (#5109)

Ask an agent for a deck, a report, an HTML page or any other file, and it is one click away on the front of the request's card in My Work, under **Deliverables**.

- **The Stop hook copies what the turn made for you** into `~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/`, content-addressed (`report-3f9a1c2b.md`), so the copy outlives the worktree, scratch folder or temp directory it was made in. Files an agent attaches through `work_state_write` (`work_product`, `deliverable`, or any field naming a file a person opens) count, as do decks, documents, pages, images, video and spreadsheets written outside the source tree. Source files are never copied by inference. SubagentStop captures what a subagent made from its own transcript.
- **The worker records and serves each copy** at `GET /api/deliverables/:id/:filename`, with the same loopback, same-origin and sandbox rules as recorded files; markdown and text open inline. While a copy is on disk and the file has not been written since, it stands in for the record of where the file was made.
- **Privacy and limits are explicit.** A turn whose prompt is entirely `<private>` leaves no copy and no record. Nothing is copied for a worker on another host, which could not open the copy. 50 files per Stop and 512 MiB per file, reported when hit, never silent. `CLAUDE_MEM_DELIVERABLES_ENABLED=false` turns the copy off.
- The SessionStart work-state rule now asks agents to write the thing you asked for as a file and attach it as `work_product` before they finish.

### Also new

- **Automatic local database snapshots** with crash-safe restore: `npx claude-mem backup [run|status|list]` and `npx claude-mem restore`. Off by default; `CLAUDE_MEM_BACKUP_ENABLED=true` with `CLAUDE_MEM_BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS` and `CLAUDE_MEM_BACKUP_RETAIN_COUNT`. (#3751)
- **Notion export.** Each new observation is upserted into a Notion database as soon as it is stored. Opt-in through `CLAUDE_MEM_NOTION_ENABLED`, a token and a database id; never blocks capture. (#4799)
- **Codex subagents start with the memory timeline.** A new `SubagentStart` hook gives a fresh subagent the same context SessionStart gives a session; forks, which inherit their parent's history, are skipped. Codex asks once to trust the new hook. (#4760)
- **Runcrate preset** for the openai-compatible provider. (#5067)

### Fixes

- **Antigravity CLI:** claude-mem no longer registers `PreToolUse`, which auto-approved every agy tool call and queued each call twice (#5085). agy prompts are now recorded once per turn, so agy work shows up in My Work, and files read in agy get their observation history (#5092).
- **Redaction:** temporary AWS credentials are redacted in full: ASIA access key IDs, session tokens, and the SecretAccessKey in `aws sts` JSON output (#5066, #5073, #5080).
- **Transcripts:** watcher checkpoints are held until buffered work is stored (#5072); the transcript-watch config path follows `CLAUDE_MEM_DATA_DIR` (#5070).
- **Observer parser:** reads the type the model settled on, never markup around it (#5077).
- **Windows:** the launcher compiles through the 8.3 short path when `bun.exe` is on a non-ASCII path (#5089).
- **SessionStart** terminal preview leaves room for its footer (#5084); install help says which providers need a cmem.ai sign-in (#5086).
- **Release tooling:** every shipped plugin manifest carries the same version, synced by the build and checked in CI (#5083, #5082, #5075).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.2.1...v15.3.0

## What's Changed
### 🚨 Security
* Improve MCP startup compatibility and lazy-load CLI commands by @Shockang in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/207
* test: add integration test coverage and fix KuzuDB fork crashes by @magyargergo in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/209
### 🚀 Features
* feat(hooks): auto-reindex after git commit with embeddings preservation by @L1nusB in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/205
* feat: HTTP embedding backend for self-hosted/remote endpoints by @zm2231 in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/395

* feat: add docker support by @BRAINIFII in https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/848
### 🐛 Bug Fixes

name: graphify 0.9.96
body:
## 0.9.96 (2026-10-25)

- Security: **deps** the Pillow floor is raised to `>=13.0.0` on Python 3.11+ (staying at `>=12.3.0` on 3.10, which Pillow 13 no longer supports) and pypdf to `>=6.19.0`, and the lockfile is refreshed to patched versions of transitive dependencies (pyjwt, cryptography, certifi, urllib3, anyio, fsspec, soupsieve, virtualenv). This clears the bulk of the open Dependabot advisories; the Pillow image-parsing CVEs are only patched upstream for Python 3.11+, so a 3.10 install keeps the newest 3.10-compatible Pillow.
- Fix: **llm** a chunk that failed before returning a response no longer has its files reported as model omissions; the warning distinguishes a failed chunk from a genuine omission, and both are still re-dispatched (#3616, #4752, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @GREYGROUPJP).
- Fix: **watch** a Markdown file that `detect()` classifies as a paper (arXiv markers, an Abstract) is included in the watch quick-scan rebuild instead of contributing zero nodes; a paper that already has a semantic layer is still excluded from the AST quick-scan (#4750, #4751, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @yeochul-jeon).
- Fix: **prs** every unfinished CheckRun status (`WAITING`, `REQUESTED`, `PENDING`, ...) counts as pending CI, so a PR gated on a deployment-protection job is no longer read as ready (#4730, thanks @rudycelekli).
- Fix: **export** an Obsidian note lists every parallel relation between two nodes (for example both `imports` and `calls`) instead of only the first edge (#4731, thanks @rudycelekli).
- Fix: **build** a hyperedge whose members are given under the `members`/`node_ids` aliases has its numeric member ids coerced to strings like the canonical `nodes` list, so the hyperedge is no longer dropped (#4732, thanks @rudycelekli).
- Fix: **llm** a code node whose confidence is written in a different case (`extracted`/`Extracted`) is still evidence-checked before it folds to the `EXTRACTED` enum, so an un-verified node is not presented as solid (#4733, thanks @rudycelekli).
- Fix: **python** a member call binds to the method it actually spells rather than a case/underscore-folded twin (`run()` no longer resolves to `_run()`); a lone folded method still resolves, and a genuine collision fails closed (#4734, thanks @rudycelekli).
- Fix: **zig** a call no longer crosses between a method and a same-named free function; a bare call binds the free function and a receiver call binds the method (#4755, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **dart** an unnamed `extension on T { }` declaration is detected and extracted (the name is optional), so its members attach to the extended type (#4741, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **llm** the DeepSeek backend sends its output cap as `max_tokens` (which DeepSeek honours) rather than `max_completion_tokens` (which it ignores), so responses are no longer silently uncapped (#4739, #4753, thanks @Ethereal49; reported by @snapp-kenya).
- Fix: **extract** XAML codebehind (`*.xaml` to `*.xaml.cs`) resolves deterministically regardless of directory iteration order, so a graph built on a case-sensitive filesystem is stable (#4747, thanks @anishraja04).
- Fix: **extract** the AST cache hit rate is reported over the file total, not the uncached set, so a warm run no longer prints a misleading "100% uncached" line (#4740, #4746, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @lavaxun).
- Fix: **dedup** a node id legitimately shared by two files as a `module`/`namespace` no longer prints a spurious "minted by two different files" warning (#4756, thanks @idachev).
- Fix: **python** the member-call resolver binds only Python callers to Python targets, so a same-named class in another language is no longer mis-bound as a call (#4757, thanks @idachev).
- Fix: **cli** the PreToolUse hook reminders are worded as facts rather than imperatives, so the agent's tool-result stream no longer reads them as prompt injection and ignores them (#2202, #4764, thanks @smngvlkz).
- Fix: **llm** the Ollama context window is sized from an estimate that counts non-Latin characters as whole tokens and from the real system-prompt length, so a non-English or long prompt is no longer silently truncated (#4414, #4761, thanks @smngvlkz).
- Fix: **cli** `graphify extract` records each run's token usage to `graphify-out/cost.json` (the same ledger the skill writes), so a standalone extract refresh updates the cost history (#1769, #4765, thanks @smngvlkz).
- Fix: **ts** chained TypeScript decorators (`@(Link().toMany())`) are recovered as a decorator reference, and a lossy-parse warning names the real error region (#4711, #4715, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **js** a `const X = require('pkg')` binding for an external package keeps its node (with the package as source) so `new X()` still resolves, while a require of a corpus-local file still folds to the required module (#4688, #4702, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **detect** generated MSBuild `obj/` and `bin/` output is pruned only when build evidence is present (restore/runtime markers nearby), so a C# project scanned after a build no longer ingests generated sources while a real `src/bin` stays (#4742, thanks @Great-Peace).
- Fix: **watch** each watch rebuild is bounded by `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT` (default 600s, `0` disables), with a thread-Timer fallback where `SIGALRM` is unavailable or `watch()` runs off the main thread (a `SIGALRM` arm there raises `ValueError` and would tear the watcher down before the rebuild ran), so a hung rebuild no longer stalls the watcher (#2173, #4724, thanks @danieldutu).
- Fix: **robot** each duplicate test-case name gets its own node (salted by line), so two tests with the same name are kept distinct (#4697, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **vbnet** external namespaces and types emit a sourceless stub carrying an empty `source_file` sentinel like other languages, instead of a node that fails validation (#4725, #4728, thanks @madanlalit; reported by @alopezradicle).
- Fix: **rust** a `use` is scoped to the crate it names, so `use serde_json::Value` no longer resolves to a same-named type in another crate; a named `pub use` re-export is followed and a manifest-less binding stays `INFERRED` (#4699, #4712, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: **python** a call through a field injected from a constructor parameter, or through a local typed by a method's return annotation, resolves to the target method (`INFERRED`); it requires a single unambiguous producer and class (#4726, thanks @keny11300).
- Fix: **dedup** an LLM-marked cross-document reference stub that collides with its real definition is namespaced instead of silently dropped, so neither node is lost (#4738, #4743, thanks @SinghAman21; reported by @snapp-kenya).
- Perf: **update** a `graphify update` with no relevant input change skips the detect/extract/build pipeline and leaves the outputs untouched, keyed on the scan file-set, config, `.graphifyrc`, extractor epoch, and an output-completeness stamp; a scanned file with no manifest row (including one whose extraction previously failed) still forces a full rebuild so a later fix is never skipped (#4740, #4748, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @lavaxun).

name: Skill 4.8.0
body:
- **Devin and Replit Agent.** `npx impeccable install` sets the skill up for Devin on the web, in the CLI and on Desktop, and accepts `windsurf` as another name for it. A project with a `.replit` file is read as Replit Agent, so the installer names it, not Codex CLI, when it writes to `.agents`. Thanks to @faocampo and @Kodylow for asking.

- **Findings on the pull request.** In a GitHub Actions job, `impeccable detect --github` turns each finding into an annotation on the line that caused it. `--list-rules` prints every rule with its category and description, and `--scope` or `--no-advisory` narrows the list. Thanks to @mvanhorn for both.

- **A second look at hard offset shadows.** A crisp shadow pushed 4px or more is flagged as an advisory, not a failure, because it can be a deliberate neobrutalist choice. Keep one with `data-impeccable-ignore="hard-offset-shadow"`. Thanks to @mager for the contribution.

- **Cursor checks the edit it just made.** The design hook runs after each write instead of gating it, with one scan per edit. `update` and `doctor --fix` move an existing hook over.

- **Hooks find your projects.** A session started in a folder above your projects now gets the end-of-session review for each project it edited. Codex hooks in your user folder are detected, and `doctor` checks their launcher. Thanks to @Shandy1972v.

- **Checked engine downloads.** The launcher, the npm package and `install` compare each engine download with a list of digests committed alongside the skill, not one published next to the file, and refuse a binary that does not match. Thanks to @jojig-dao for the design.

- **Installs that hold up.** A slow download waits as long as data keeps arriving, instead of failing at 120 seconds. If an update cannot reach the bundle, your installed skills stay as they are. Every Windows `.cmd` ships with CRLF line endings, Copilot global hooks work on Windows, and the commands Impeccable prints run in PowerShell.

- **Live mode.** Tune values survive closing the panel and reloading the page (thanks to @mager). Patching a page's Content-Security-Policy meta tag no longer corrupts the file, and phones no longer raise the keyboard when live mode loads.

- **Fewer false alarms.** `straggler` measures the last word instead of estimating it, and sees a `text-wrap: pretty` that Firefox dropped (thanks to @stedmanhalliday for both). `design-system-radius` no longer reads the numbers inside `calc()`, `min()` or `max()` as radii (thanks to @iamceph). Text dimmed by a stepper's resting state is an advisory, while text a script parked mid-reveal still counts. In a monorepo, each file's design tokens come from its own package first. A negative value in a margin shorthand is no longer lost. Legal and footnote blocks are exempt from line length and tiny text. URL scans skip cookie notices, splash gates and hidden mockups, and contrast reads gradient text and dark surfaces correctly. Images set through `srcset` count, and `cramped-padding` sees through a transparent wrapper (thanks to @BibaPutt).

- **Side stripes on table rows.** A colored stripe down one side of a status row or cell now reports as a side tab, in URL scans as well as file scans, and an `!important` reset stands it down.

- **Arabic-script text.** `harden` now covers ZWNJ, Yeh and Kaf variants, local digits and calendars for Arabic-script languages. Thanks to @FawwazLawal.

- **Fixes.** Ask for more directions than the weighing supports and new work shows the ones that earned a place and says so, instead of padding the hand (thanks to @tehzunm-ctrl). `**/` in an ignore pattern stops at folder boundaries, so one waiver no longer skips an unrelated page. Live mode starts in a page that blocks storage. Audit's contrast and touch-target checks match WCAG AA. Thanks to @srobroek.

name: CLI 4.8.0
body:
- **GitHub Actions annotations.** `--github` prints each finding as an annotation on the line that caused it. Thanks to @mvanhorn. 
`npx impeccable@latest detect --github src/`
- **The rule list.** `--list-rules` prints every rule without scanning, as text or `--json`. - **Devin and Replit Agent.** `install` accepts `devin` and `windsurf`, and names Replit Agent when a project has a `.replit` file. - **Steadier installs.** `install` and `update` wait on an idle connection instead of a fixed 120 seconds, and an update with no network keeps the skills you have. The engine binary is checked against digests committed with the package before it runs. - **The current detector.** Engine 0.1.18 brings the hard offset shadow advisory and every accuracy fix in skill v4.8.0.

name: 0.13.14: Python agent and integration updates
body:
This release keeps the Python agent and its existing models. The Pi migration remains separate.

Changes since the last PyPI release:
- Add OpenAI browser tools and the shared Bash helper.
- Improve bounded page observations, form state, file access, and browser recovery.
- Fix temporary empty Cloud tab URLs.
- Keep screenshots, crops, and clicks aligned on scaled displays.
- Clean up failed browser reconnect initialization.
- Improve missing-key errors for Cloud browsers.
- Support Browser Use Cloud SDK V4 imports.
- Update aiohttp from 3.14.3 to 3.14.5.
- Refresh Cloud guidance and saved-task replay examples.

Validation:
- GitHub checks pass on the exact release source.
- Pre-commit passes for the version change.
- The wheel and source package build successfully.
- Package metadata and all five CLI entries pass validation.
- All 171 packaged Python files match the existing Python runtime.
- The installed wheel runs `browser-use --help`.

Install with `uv add browser-use==0.13.14` or `pip install browser-use==0.13.14`.

The protected publishing workflow requires another release reviewer. PyPI publication follows that approval.
